newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BANKS SHOULD SEEK SOLUTIONS BEFORE EMU - PANTALAKIS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BANKS SHOULD SEEK SOLUTIONS BEFORE EMU - PANTALAKIS.

text.p: Greek banks should try to find solutions before problems arising from the EMU and the introduction of Euro, state National Bank deputy governor Theodore Pantalakis told the Economist conference.
"The transition to the EMU does not require just the adjustment of information systems and software applications that each bank uses," said Pantalakis.

Action should be taken to solve legal problems related to the continuity of existing contracts and cash flows, the needed reforms in money and capital markets and the change in the framework of conducting monetary policy and payments systems, he said.

Greek banks will face a higher cost from Greece's delayed entry into the EMU because they will have to cope with costs and risks that their competitors will not have to face, he added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
